{
  "research_question": "How does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": "Success rates and Path Efficiency are highest in the Bright Visual Only (78.5%, 50.4%) and Combined (78.0%, 50.2%) groups, significantly outperforming the Sham group (27.3% success, 30.8% path efficiency). Time-to-Target is fastest in Combined (2.56s) and Bright Visual Only (2.61s), while Sham mice take significantly longer (4.68s). Average Speed is slightly higher in Combined (12.83) and Bright Visual Only (12.68) compared to Sham (10.74). Angular Dispersion (AD) indicates that Combined and Bright Visual Only groups show the most spread out paths (mean AD ~0.40), whereas the Sham group shows the tightest clustering of paths (mean AD 0.24).",
  "strongest_group_differences": "The most stark difference is in the Success rate, where the Combined and Bright Visual Only groups (approx. 0.78) are nearly three times more successful than the Sham group (0.27). Similarly, Time-to-Target shows the largest gap between Sham (4.68s) and the active stimulation groups (2.56s - 3.14s), indicating Sham mice are significantly slower to reach the target. Path Efficiency also shows a large deficit in the Sham group (0.31) compared to all other paradigms (0.43 - 0.50).",
  "practical_interpretation": "Active stimulation paradigms, particularly those involving visual input (Bright Visual Only) or combined inputs, drastically improve navigation success and speed compared to Sham controls. Successful navigation in active groups is accompanied by longer, more exploratory paths (higher Path Efficiency, higher AD), suggesting mice are actively searching the environment rather than failing to reach the target. The Sham group's poor performance (low success, low speed) combined with low AD suggests they may be failing to navigate effectively or are restricted to a small area, unable to locate the target within the experimental timeframe.",
  "limitations": "The analysis relies solely on summary statistics (mean, SD) without access to individual data points or raw distributions, preventing the calculation of effect sizes, confidence intervals, or formal statistical significance tests (e.g., ANOVA, t-tests). The data represents a single run (Replication 1), so the generalizability of these findings across different experimental sessions or models is unknown. Outliers (e.g., Time-to-Target max 201.4) are not analyzed individually to determine if they skew the means.",
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test for each of the five response variables to determine statistical significance between the five stimulation paradigm groups. Calculate effect sizes (e.g., Cohen's d or eta-squared) to quantify the magnitude of the differences. Perform post-hoc pairwise comparisons with corrections for multiple comparisons (e.g., Tukey HSD) to identify exactly which groups differ from one another. Analyze the relationship between Success and Time-to-Target within each paradigm to understand failure modes."
}
